currentContext.business: The Company designs and manufactures scientific research and laboratory instrumentation spanning imaging, measuring, spectroscopy and analytical instruments, physics laboratory equipment, opto-mechanics and optics, breadboards/tabletops/rails and overhead shelves, linear and rotation stages (manual and motorised) and industrial automation. It sells to IITs and research institutions, universities and IISERs, government e-marketplace (GeM) and formal tenders, and private customers such as pharmaceutical companies, supported by a dealer network in India and overseas. It also offers end-to-end optical manufacturing under OPTOFab, covering design, fabrication, alignment, testing and performance evaluation of high-precision optical components, opto-mechanical systems and custom optical assemblies.

Optical manufacturing capability: OPTOFab (design, fabrication, alignment, testing and performance evaluation of high-precision optical components and custom optical assemblies)

risks.risk: Export exposure to tariffs and geopolitical conflict
risks.note: The imposition of higher tariffs by the United States and continuing conflicts in the Middle East have adversely impacted the Company's export business by affecting international trade, logistics and supply chains; geopolitical disruption is also listed among SWOT threats for freight and supply chains.

risks.risk: Price competition from low-cost imports and unorganised local manufacturers
risks.note: Increasing competition from low-cost products imported from China, plus unorganised local manufacturers offering cheap products, intensifies price competition and poses quality-related challenges in the market.

risks.risk: Affordability-driven procurement in the academic segment
risks.note: In the academic segment procurement decisions are often driven by affordability rather than advanced features, which may limit adoption of the Company's high-end scientific instruments — relevant given the concentration of tender activity in IITs, research institutions, universities and IISERs.

risks.risk: Shortage of skilled talent and workforce retention
risks.note: A shortage of skilled professionals to operate and maintain sophisticated systems, together with changing attitudes towards work and talent retention, is flagged both as a business risk and as a SWOT weakness/threat for a technology-intensive manufacturer.

risks.risk: Rising operational costs and high capital/maintenance cost of advanced technologies
risks.note: Management lists rising operational costs among its business risks, while high capital investment and maintenance costs associated with advanced technologies are cited as a weakness.

Complex and evolving regulatory and compliance requirements are flagged both in Risks & Concerns and as a SWOT weakness; CSR obligations under Section 135 also become applicable from FY2026-27 as the Company has now met the prescribed net-profit threshold.

Delayed adoption and integration of Artificial Intelligence technologies is listed as a weakness in a market where AI, automation and digitalisation are the stated growth drivers for scientific research equipment.
Irregular power supply is flagged as a threat affecting manufacturing operations and productivity.

hero.oneLiner: Holmarc Opto-Mechatronics is an Indian manufacturer of scientific research, laboratory and opto-mechanical instruments, supplying research institutions, universities and, increasingly, the private pharmaceutical sector in India and export markets.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Holmarc Opto-Mechatronics is an Indian manufacturer of scientific research, laboratory and opto-mechanical instruments, supplying research institutions, universities and, increasingly, the private pharmaceutical sector in India and export markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company designs and manufactures scientific research and laboratory instrumentation spanning imaging, measuring, spectroscopy and analytical instruments, physics laboratory equipment, opto-mechanics and optics, breadboards/tabletops/rails and overhead shelves, linear and rotation stages (manual and motorised) and industrial automation. It sells to IITs and research institutions, universities and IISERs, government e-marketplace (GeM) and formal tenders, and private customers such as pharmaceutical companies, supported by a dealer network in India and overseas. It also offers end-to-end optical manufacturing under OPTOFab, covering design, fabrication, alignment, testing and performance evaluation of high-precision optical components, opto-mechanical systems and custom optical assemblies.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- M/s. Cyriac and Cyriac — related party: Firm in which Mr. Jolly Cyriac's brother is a partner; provides legal retainership services covering litigation and non-litigation matters, legal opinions, vetting of agreements/contracts and quarterly statutory-compliance inspections. Contract at arm's length, terminable upon notice.
- IHits Technologies Private Limited — related party: Private company (CIN U72200KL2014PTC036787) in which Mr. Jolly Cyriac's brother is a director; the Company avails Human Resource Management software services and their implementation. Contract at arm's length, running till 31/03/2026.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Disclosed product categories:** Imaging Instruments, Measuring Instruments, Spectroscopy, Analytical Instruments, Lab Equipments, Physics Lab Equipments, Breadboards/tabletops/rails and carriers/Overhead shelf, Opto-mechanics, Optics, Linear and Rotation stages, Motorized Linear and rotation stages, Industrial Automation
- **Named instruments introduced or supplied during FY26:** Hyperspectral NIR Camera, Industrial Scale Needle-less Electrospinning Unit, Doctor Blade Thin Film Applicator, Digital Inverted Microscope, Motorized Digital Inverted Microscope, Rheo-Optics Set-up, Optical Microscope Segment System, Inverted Metallurgical Microscope, Vacuum Compatible X-ray Crystal Assembly
- **Optical manufacturing capability:** OPTOFab (design, fabrication, alignment, testing and performance evaluation of high-precision optical components and custom optical assemblies)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- IITs and research institutions (largest tender category)
- Universities and IISERs
- Government procurement via GeM and e-tenders
- Private pharmaceutical and biotechnology customers (e.g. Bharat Biotech International Limited)
- Academic segment, where procurement is often affordability-driven
- Dealer network of 71 dealers in India and 23 dealers overseas
- Exports: France, Spain, Kenya, UAE, Israel and China (growth); United States (moderate decline due to higher tariffs)
- New export markets added: Mexico, the Netherlands, South Africa, Slovakia and Sweden
- Big-science programme supply: ITER-India

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Company anticipates strong growth in the coming years, supported by the Government of India's increased focus on R&D under the 'Viksit Bharat 2047' vision
- Steady growth in the Indian scientific research equipment market driven by rising R&D activity in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare and academic sectors
- Government support programmes cited as demand drivers — PLI Scheme for pharmaceuticals and medical devices, Make in India, National Mission on Quantum Technologies & Applications, Atmanirbhar Bharat, the National Medical Devices Policy 2023, and over 2,100 Global Capability Centres
- India's shift beyond generic pharma into drug discovery, biologics, vaccines, Cell and Gene Therapy and Antibody-Drug Conjugates, driving demand for sophisticated laboratory and analytical instruments
- Global research base as a demand pool — more than 300,000 research laboratories and over 20,000 drug candidates under development worldwide
- Advances in spectroscopy (THz, 2D, SERS, CARS) and adoption of handheld/portable spectrometers extending applications beyond the laboratory
- Analytical instruments market growth driven by automation, AI, microtechnology and Lab-on-a-Chip platforms opening point-of-care and field-based applications
- Growing number of Contract Research Organizations in India creating increased demand for scientific research equipment
- DRDO's strategic focus on self-reliance and industry collaboration, creating opportunity for indigenous scientific equipment manufacturers
- Rising demand for solid and honeycomb breadboards, workstations and optical tables for research and laboratory infrastructure
- Dealer-network sales continue to improve and the Company expects further growth in the coming years
- Headwinds flagged: higher US tariffs and Middle East conflicts hurting exports, low-cost Chinese imports intensifying price competition, unorganised local manufacturers, and affordability-driven procurement in the academic segment limiting adoption of high-end instruments
- FY26 growth concentrated in Physics Laboratory Equipment (18.92%) and Breadboards, Tabletops and Rails (28.62%)
- Participated in 5,860 tenders and enquiries floated by organisations across India during the year and secured 1,974 orders, a success rate of 33.69%
- Tender conversion by channel: IITs & research institutions 596 of 1,648 (36.16%); Universities & IISERs 444 of 1,512 (29.36%); GeM 55 of 87 (63.21%); E-tenders 66 of 104 (63.46%); Dealers 578 of 1,757 (32.9%); Export 176 of 661 (26.62%); Formal 59 of 91 (64.83%)
- Received an order from ITER-India for the supply of a Vacuum Compatible X-ray Crystal Assembly, described as a milestone strengthening its association with the ITER programme
- Entered into 11 Non-Disclosure Agreements during the year, including one with Merck Life KGaA, Germany for development of an analytical instrument and one with Vital Biosciences Inc., Canada for development of an automated dispensing unit

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continuous product development — expanding the product portfolio with innovative instruments such as the Hyperspectral NIR Camera, Industrial Scale Needle-less Electrospinning Unit and Doctor Blade Thin Film Applicator
- Introduction of hyperspectral imaging systems, targeted at defence, agriculture and industrial applications
- Expansion into the private sector, particularly the pharmaceutical industry, beyond the traditional academic and research base
- Growing the dealer-led distribution model — 71 dealers in India and 23 overseas, with sales through the network continuing to improve
- Active participation in major exhibitions in India and abroad to enhance business growth and market presence (11 national exhibitions and ARABLAB in FY26)
- Expanding advanced optical manufacturing capabilities under OPTOFab — end-to-end design, fabrication, alignment, testing and performance evaluation of high-precision optical components and custom optical assemblies
- Co-development with global partners under NDAs, including Merck Life KGaA (Germany) for an analytical instrument and Vital Biosciences Inc. (Canada) for an automated dispensing unit
- Indigenous product innovation in collaboration with academic institutions and government departments (Industrial Scale Needle-less Electrospinning Unit with SASTRA Deemed to be University, supported by the Ministry of Heavy Industries)
- Diversifying export geographies to offset the US tariff impact, adding Mexico, the Netherlands, South Africa, Slovakia and Sweden
- Continuous investment in research and development to drive innovation and product development
- Building a future-ready workforce through continuous learning, skill enhancement, leadership development and career growth
- Strengthening the internal control framework, with an independent Chartered Accountant's recommendations being implemented in a phased manner
- Dividend is recommended by the Board and declared by members out of the profits of the Company: for FY26 a final dividend of Rs 0.5 per equity share (5% on the Rs 10 face value) was recommended at the Board meeting held on 28th May 2026 and placed before the 34th AGM for declaration. Related-party dealings are confined to the ordinary course of business at arm's length, with no material or non-arm's-length contracts reported.
- Corporate Social Responsibility under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 was not applicable during FY26, but the Company has met the prescribed net-profit threshold based on the audited FY26 financial statements and CSR provisions will apply from FY2026-27
- In-house Risk Management procedure under Section 134(3)(n) identifying elements of risk that may threaten the existence of the Company, with major risks addressed and monitored by the Board of Directors
- Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy for directors and employees, overseen by the Audit Committee with direct access to its Chairman and safeguards against victimisation; policy published on the Company website; no complaints filed or pending during the year
- Internal Complaints Committees constituted at each workplace under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013; nil complaints pending at the start of the year, nil received, nil disposed and nil cases pending beyond ninety days
- Affirmed compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, with measures taken to adhere to statutory requirements for women employees
- Conservation of energy and technology absorption disclosure under Section 134(3)(m) filed as Annexure 4 to the Directors' Report
- No frauds occurred or were reported by the Auditors during the period; no transactions fraudulent, illegal or in violation of the Company's Code of Conduct
- No significant or material orders were passed by regulators, courts or tribunals impacting the going-concern status or future operations, and no application was made or proceeding pending under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
- Related-party transactions were in the ordinary course of business at arm's length, none exceeding the Rule 15 thresholds or qualifying as material RPTs under SEBI LODR, so shareholder approval was not required
- The Company is not obligated to comply with the Corporate Governance provisions of Regulation 15(2) of SEBI LODR, but states it follows best corporate governance practices; Secretarial Standards for Board and General Meetings were complied with

risks.body:

- Price competition from low-cost imports and unorganised local manufacturers — Increasing competition from low-cost products imported from China, plus unorganised local manufacturers offering cheap products, intensifies price competition and poses quality-related challenges in the market.

- Shortage of skilled talent and workforce retention — A shortage of skilled professionals to operate and maintain sophisticated systems, together with changing attitudes towards work and talent retention, is flagged both as a business risk and as a SWOT weakness/threat for a technology-intensive manufacturer.
- Rising operational costs and high capital/maintenance cost of advanced technologies — Management lists rising operational costs among its business risks, while high capital investment and maintenance costs associated with advanced technologies are cited as a weakness.

- Technology-adoption lag, particularly in AI — Delayed adoption and integration of Artificial Intelligence technologies is listed as a weakness in a market where AI, automation and digitalisation are the stated growth drivers for scientific research equipment.
- Operating dependence on reliable power — Irregular power supply is flagged as a threat affecting manufacturing operations and productivity.
